Software Engineer, AV Frameworks – Early Career
Sunnyvale, CA
Full-time
Hybrid
New Grad
$125K/yr - $150K/yr
General Motors builds foundational frameworks for robotics and autonomous capabilities across distributed compute. The early-career Software Engineer will design and deliver core communication and runtime components for autonomous vehicle and robotics applications, focusing on C++ systems, Linux, networking, and IPC. The role also involves performance optimization, developer-facing tooling, observability, testing, and reliability improvements.
Automotive
Electric Vehicle
Information Technology
Manufacturing
Transportation
Information Services
H1B Sponsor Likely
Responsibilities
Build and debug high-performance IPC and middleware primitives (publish/subscribe, shared memory, serialization, discovery, QoS)
Drive latency, throughput, and determinism improvements through profiling, tracing, benchmarking, and targeted optimizations
Build developer-facing APIs, tooling, and documentation that improve ergonomics, correctness, and velocity for internal customers
Deliver platform-ready components with observability (metrics, logs, traces), robust fault handling, and reproducible performance characteristics
Work alongside experienced engineers platform OS, drivers, safety, controls, perception, and tooling teams to ramp up on AV software
Apply production rigor: code reviews, testing strategies (unit, integration, soak), performance and regression gates, and rollout/rollback discipline
Grow through progressively more complex assignments spanning design, implementation, integration, and testing
Qualification
Modern C++
Python

ROS 2

Required
Recently completed a BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a degree in a related field
Strong background in modern C++ (20/23) and Python development, demonstrated through coursework, internships, research, or substantial projects
Strong grasp of software fundamentals including concurrency, memory management, lock-free or low-contention patterns, and performance profiling
Hands-on experience with IPC/messaging systems and distributed systems fundamentals (serialization, backpressure, flow control, QoS)
Knowledge of linux-based networking (sockets, TCP/UDP, multicast, NICs, buffers, MTU, packetization)
Ability to debug complex software problems, reason about system behavior, and communicate clearly in a collaborative team environment
Interest in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embedded systems, or high-performance software
Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to our Suynnvale, CA office three times per week, at minimum
Preferred
Robotics/AV middleware: ROS 2, DDS, gRPC
Serialization and data: Protobuf, FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto, zero-copy techniques
Real-time Linux and systems constraints (scheduling, CPU isolation, priority inversion mitigation, bounded latency)
Prior internship, research, or project experience in autonomous driving, robotics, embedded systems, AI/ML infrastructure, or platform software
Degree completed between December 2025 and August 2026, with availability to begin employment in 2026
Benefits
This role may be eligible for relocation benefits
Hybrid work arrangement, with the successful candidate expected to report to the Sunnyvale, CA office three times per week, at minimum
An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance
